kv.memory.bcp14-keyword-discipline: Mark 2026-10-20: In DRAFTS, MUST/MUST NOT only where the protocol does not work at all without the requirement (interop breaks). Never use MUST/MUST NOT to force good practice, security hygiene, or things implementations do anyway; use SHOULD, plain prose, or cite an existing RFC MUST instead of restating it. Security/privacy/harm-limiting MUSTs (blocking, E2EE, access control/enumeration notFound, consent, credentials, SSRF) are downgraded to SHOULD too; the RFC 2119 sec 6 harm exception is NOT used. ONE EXCEPTION: federation request-signature verification and sender identity binding stay MUST (federation trust model). GUIDES: keep their keywords and their 'A note on RFC 2119 keywords' sections; only fix guide keywords that contradict a draft (different strength or content).
kv.memory.bd-create-parallel-race: Do not parallelize 'bd create --silent &' calls against the same database. The SQLite ID assignment races; two children of the same epic can collide on the same .N suffix, causing one creation to silently drop. Mitigation: chain sequential 'bd create ... && bd create ...' instead of parallel '&'. Verified during 2026-05-12 session — lost a bead in a 4-way parallel batch under epic fig9; had to recreate sequentially.
kv.memory.blocked-sender-suppression-any: Blocked-sender suppression: any new ephemeral event delivery feature in JMAP Chat (typing, presence, reactions-in-flight, read-receipts-in-flight, etc.) must include a blocked-sender check in the normative draft, not just in the guide. Pattern: if sender is on recipient's blocked list (ChatContact.blocked=true), the event MUST be silently dropped. Main draft :1473 establishes this for messages; extension to ephemeral signals prevents a blocked user from leaking presence/attention pattern. Found missing for ChatTypingEvent in WSS draft (filed as dim0); ChatPresenceEvent had it. Audit any new ephemeral type the same way.
kv.memory.chat-did-depends: Mark 2026-10-16: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did builds normatively on draft-atwood-jmap-did (requires urn:ietf:params:jmap:did; one DID lifecycle and one supportedMethods field).
kv.memory.chat-did-federation-binding: Mark 2026-10-20 confirmed: for a host-less DID peer identity, federation's single RFC 9421 Ed25519 request signature is bound to the DID by requiring the verifying key (peerSigningKeys entry named by keyid) to be in the DID Document's authentication relationship (octet compare). Consequences accepted: server holds an authentication key of that DID (keyCustody cannot be 'user'); for did:key, rotating the server key changes the DID (a migration). No second per-request DID signature. Re-resolution on key miss capped at once per 60 s (SHOULD).
kv.memory.chat-filenode-rights: Mark 2026-10-20 (nj1j), updated 2026-11-02 for spec ebdf95e (filenode-19): Space file tree rights are reported in myRights of EVERY Directory incl. the root, no root exception: view=mayRead; send=+mayAddChildren; manage_channels or manage_space=+mayDelete,mayRename,mayModifyContent. Files/SymLinks take rights from their parent Directory (no own myRights). Root protection is a separate rule, not reduced flags: no member can destroy, rename or move the root via FileNode/set; only Space destruction removes it. The draft currently grounds that on filenode rejecting destroy/rename/move of any Directory with a role; if the chatspace role is dropped (jmap-chat-spec-8g3r), state the root rule directly. crate-jmap enforces it independently (check_space_update/check_space_destroy, d92dd316; no-op restate allowed, 5a44a29a). NO role gets mayShare (server rejects shareWith changes on Space-tree nodes with forbidden). No per-uploader rights: send members cannot overwrite even their own uploads.
kv.memory.fig9-broadcast-mention-storage: fig9 broadcast-mention storage: per-user mentions stay in Message.mentions; broadcast-scope mentions in Message.broadcastMentions (new array; defaults to []); rich-body uses 'mention' span (userId) and new 'broadcast' span (scope). When bodyType is application/jmap-chat-rich, BOTH Message.mentions AND Message.broadcastMentions MUST be empty. Push computation for mentionScopes (fig9.4) must UNION over Message.broadcastMentions[].scope AND rich-body 'broadcast' spans .scope — same dual-path pattern as f86f4f4's hasMention fix for user mentions in ex4u. The 'mention_all' permission was renamed to 'mention_broadcast' in the main draft as part of fig9.2.
kv.memory.fm-cli-reply: Mark 2026-11-01: threaded replies from mark@reviewcommit.com. fm 'draft reply' always uses the primary identity fallenpegasus@fastmail.fm and has no --from; ANY 'fm draft edit' (even without --from) drops In-Reply-To/References (thread id changes). Working method: create the draft via JMAP API with FASTMAIL_TOKEN (in env; never print it): Email/get source messageId+references, Email/set create in Drafts mailbox with from/to/cc/subject/inReplyTo/references/bodyValues, then verify with 'fm email read' plus Email/get inReplyTo/references, then 'fm draft send ID --unsafe --yes'. For sends Mark has explicitly approved, use: fm draft send <id> --unsafe --yes. kv.memory.graph-federation-no: Mark 2026-10-20: graph federation is a NO until someone has a good model. Do not propose or draft it. Reasoning: single-home federation (Wave host model / ActivityPub origin / one Matrix room: one hosting server orders and stores each Graph, remote users act as participants) is understood engineering and would fit, but federating across owners is still research: cross-server edges (ownership, leaking node existence vs access control), cross-server referential integrity (dangling edges; only eventual repair/tombstones), federated query/traversal with partial visibility (cf. federated SPARQL, link-traversal querying), multi-authority conflict resolution (cf. Matrix state resolution), federated search ranking/freshness. Drafts keep cross-graph edges forbidden and federation out of scope (graph-00, graph-edit-00).
kv.memory.group-avatar-best-effort: Mark 2026-10-20: Peer/groupUpdate avatar is best-effort: if fetch or size/sha256 check fails, receiver applies the rest of the request and leaves avatar unset (create) or unchanged (updateMetadata); MAY retry later; never rejects (rejection is permanent; avatar cosmetic). Attachments differ: tracked as jmap-chat-spec-9wz3 (classify transient vs permanent).
kv.memory.ietf-imap-archive: IETF mailing-list archive is readable over IMAP: imap.ietf.org:993 (implicit TLS, Isode M-Box). Anonymous login: user 'anonymous', password 'mark@reviewcommit.com' (Mark's chosen anon password; always use it). AUTH=PLAIN. Read-only; ~1384 folders named 'Shared Folders/<list>', e.g. 'Shared Folders/jmap', 'Shared Folders/mimi', 'Shared Folders/mls'. Use SELECT readonly + SEARCH SINCE dd-Mon-yyyy to check for replies to list posts. Python: imaplib.IMAP4_SSL('imap.ietf.org',993). Verified 2026-11-01. kv.memory.jmap-chat-spec-kq1-r2-assessme: jmap-chat-spec-kq1 R2 assessment: 15% confidence of missed bug. Real complaints exhausted. Channel exemption (line 439) resolves P0 jmap-chat-spec-0fw.26 as design choice. Missing {#chat-typing} anchor is only residual editorial issue. No round 3 needed.
kv.memory.jmap-cid-design-decisions-1-sh: jmap-cid design decisions: (1) SHA-256 only, lowercase hex, field named sha256. No multihash/IPFS CID. Complements JMAP-BLOBEXT digest:sha-256 (base64, Blob/get) without conflict. (2) Standalone capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:cid. Sections structured to also serve as upstream patches to RFC 8620 upload response and JMAP-FILENODE FileNode object.
kv.memory.jmap-graph-design-decisions: Mark 2026-10-20: jmap-graph (draft-atwood-jmap-graph-00, urn:ietf:params:jmap:graph) is an UNOPINIONATED graph core grown from a Google-Wave idea. Standalone (not chat companion), not built on FileNode or Tasks (both opinionated; Tasks upstream expired). Types Graph/GraphNode/GraphEdge (prefixed to avoid generic JMAP Data Types registry names). Graph = unit of access (RFC 9670 shareWith; no per-node ACL), no cross-graph edges. No edge semantics, no shape constraints (cycles/multi-edges ok), no ordering (sort keys are annotations). Only integrity rule: edge endpoints exist in same graph; node destroy cascades edges. Annotations String[*], per-key PatchObject = LWW per key. Query filters structural only and require a single FilterCondition with graphId. No profiles yet. Companions: graph-projection (MAY, per-account projected Graph filtered by native rights, writes MAY with server-defined meaning) and graph-search (built-in MQL-style JSON 'where' language with JSON Pointer fields, $edge/$reachable/$from/$to, optional $text; advertised languages registry gql/opencypher/gremlin/documentdb/sparql). Still out of scope: live in-node co-editing (op log; server-sequences-never-merges, Fluid-style), WSS, federation, E2EE, profiles. Multi-hop via core filters is one request per hop (RFC 8620 result refs replace only top-level args); fromId/toId filters take Id[].
kv.memory.jmap-graph-projection-writes: Mark 2026-10-20: graph-projection writes MAY be accepted; their meaning (native change, graph-only data, nothing) is server-defined in -00. myRights server-defined per user incl. owner; mayAdmin false, shareWith null (visibility = native rights). Writes touching source objects SHOULD get native rights checks/validation/side effects. Future doc may standardize per-type write meanings.

Mark's 17 Tasks items on jmapio/jmap (PRs #458-#472, issues #456-#471) stay as-is; 'we will do what we want until it reanimates on its own in the IETF'.
kv.memory.leave-to-implementations: Mark 2026-11-02: Do not overdefine. Drafts cannot force implementations, so do not specify mechanisms for access control, sharing, presentation, or storage policy beyond what interop needs. Default posture: state what each object is for, grant permissive MAYs, rely on existing RFC rules (e.g. RFC 8620 blob access). Applied 2026-11-02 to FileNode+SpaceFile coexistence, number of Space roots (0/1/more), and blob download access (no blob ACL rule, no bead). Do not propose new access-control rules unless Mark asks. Complements bcp14-keyword-discipline.
kv.memory.mention-information-is-stored-: Mention information is stored in TWO places in JMAP Chat depending on bodyType: (1) Message.mentions array (Mention[]) for text/plain and text/markdown; (2) inline spans of type 'mention' with userId field for application/jmap-chat-rich (Message.mentions MUST be empty in that case per main draft :1257). Any cross-document rule that 'checks Message.mentions' is silently wrong for rich-body. Affects push hasMention (filed as ex4u), and likely other places to audit: notification/badge logic, mention queries, federation Peer/deliver mention extraction. fig9.4 (broadcast-mention scope) adds a third storage dimension.
kv.memory.push-draft-mentionscopes-is-pe: Push draft mentionScopes is PER-RECIPIENT, not per-message. Server computes the candidate set from Message.broadcastMentions[].scope UNION rich-body 'broadcast' spans .scope, then filters to scopes for which the receiving account owner is in the locally-resolved recipient set. This is what makes mentionUrgency elevation correct for @here and @admins where only some recipients qualify under the deployment's predicate. A non-targeted recipient of an @here message gets mentionScopes:[] and does NOT get mentionUrgency elevation. Field added in fig9.4 commit replacing the old hasMentionAll boolean.
kv.memory.push-shared-checkout: 2026-11-02 lesson: before pushing a repo another Claude session works in (e.g. ~/PROJECT/crate-jmap), check 'git rev-list --count origin/main..main'. If it is more than the commits you made, STOP and ask Mark: 'git push origin main' pushes the other session's unpushed local commits too. On 11-02 a beads-only push to crate-jmap carried 4 of another session's commits (df5a2d7b..5a44a29a) to origin without Mark's approval. Commit only your own .beads files there; leave the other session's bead files and counter.json/last-touched.
kv.memory.spec-reference-library: Local IETF/W3C reference library: ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs (README.md there). ~880 RFC files (rfcNNNN.txt for <=8649, .xml+.txt for >=8650), I-D XML masters (draft-WG-topic-VV.xml), W3C ReSpec sources (w3c-*.html), WHATWG .bs, NIST/ITU PDFs, ulid-spec.md. Read spec text there before going to the network; it is a snapshot, so check datatracker / W3C TR for the current version. kramdown-rfc is at ~/.local/share/gem/ruby/3.2.0/bin/kramdown-rfc (not on PATH); xml2rfc is on PATH.
kv.memory.typing-notifications-nearly-ev: Typing notifications: nearly everything about them should use SHOULD/MAY not MUST/SHALL. They are best-effort ephemeral signals, not reliable protocol obligations.
kv.memory.urn-ietf-params-jmap: Mark 2026-10-20: urn:jmap: was a mistake. All corpus capability URNs and the chat MessageAction/Endpoint types use the RFC 8620 sec 9.3 sub-namespace urn:ietf:params:jmap: (bead k16o). The corpus assigns names there ONLY via the JMAP Capabilities registry: capabilities plus placeholder urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap: (RFC 8620 9.4.7 model); names under the placeholder are assigned only by Standards Track RFCs. Object references are NOT URNs (RFC 3553 forbids non-persistent ids in names): they are JMAP object URIs in the jmap: URI scheme, jmap:<type-name>:<accountId>:<objectId>, defined + registered (RFC 7595, Permanent) in standalone draft-atwood-jmap-object-uri-00 ({{JMAP-OBJECT-URI}}); registry 'JMAP Object URI Types' (Type Name, Data Type, Reference), no initial entries; calendars/tasks/graph-projection register their types. jmap:// forms reserved for future. Context-relative, not globally unique. No collision rule with capabilities. graph-projection property is objectUri. chat-filenode root role is plain token 'chatspace' (not a URN).
kv.memory.zulip-openmls: Mark 2026-11-01: openmls Zulip (https://openmls.zulipchat.com) creds are in ~/.zuliprc (chmod 600, [api] email/key/site). Drive it via REST /api/v1 with Basic auth email:key; never print the key. Channels: Bugs, Deployments & integrations, general, js. Every post needs Mark's explicit approval, like emails.
